insurer: Aditya Birla Health Insurance Co. Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (varies by Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table)

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: (9) Super Reload: What is covered We shall provide for a Reload of the Sum Insured, unlimited times during the Policy Year... (iii) The Super Reload of Sum Insured shall be available for all subsequent claims also and to any Illness / Injury (including its complications) for which a claim has been admitted for the Insured Person during that Policy Year.
great.explanation: Provides an unlimited reload of Sum Insured during the policy year, and it can be used even for the same illness/injury (including complications) after a claim is admitted. This can significantly reduce the chance of running out of cover in a high-claim year.

great.name: Bariatric Surgery
great.quote: (12) Obesity Treatment: What is Covered We shall cover the related Medical Expenses... if the Insured Person is hospitalized for a Bariatric Surgery which is medically necessary...
great.explanation: Covers medical expenses for medically necessary bariatric surgery when hospitalization is required. This is valuable because many retail health plans exclude or tightly restrict obesity surgery.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: 2. Specified disease / procedure waiting period: ... excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with Us.
good.explanation: Specified diseases/procedures are not covered until 24 months of continuous coverage are completed. Claims for listed conditions in the first 2 years will be rejected even if you are otherwise covered.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: 3. 30-day waiting period ... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are excluded for the first 30 days from policy start, except for accidents. This is a standard waiting period, so early non-accident hospitalizations may not be payable.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: (8) Reload of Sum Insured: ... Reload of Sum Insured shall be available only once during a Policy Year... (iii) ... not in relation to any Illness / Injury ... for which a claim has been admitted ... during that Policy Year.
good.reference: Section C.I.(8) Reload of Sum Insured
good.explanation: Allows one reload in a policy year, but it cannot be used for the same illness/injury for which a claim was already admitted in that year. This helps for a second unrelated hospitalization, but won’t help if the same condition recurs.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Reasonable and Customary Charges for Room Rent... up to the limits as specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table... If the Insured Person is admitted in a room category / limit that is higher... then the Insured Person shall bear a rateable proportion of the Room Rent (and the total Associated Medical Expenses...)
bad.reference: Section C.I.(1) In-patient Hospitalization (What is covered + Conditions)
bad.explanation: Room rent is limited as per the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table, and choosing a higher room category triggers a rateable (proportionate) deduction on associated medical expenses. This can sharply reduce claim payout even when your Sum Insured is sufficient.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: In case of treatment taken in a city, in a Zone higher than the eligible Zone for the Insured Person, the Co-payment percentages as below shall apply: ... Zone I ... 10% ... 15% ... 25%
bad.reference: Section C.I.(20) Co-payment for treatment in a Higher Zone + Zone Classification (Section E.II.22)
bad.explanation: A co-pay of 10% to 25% applies if treatment is taken in a higher zone than the insured person’s eligible zone. This means you must pay that percentage of each admissible claim amount out of pocket in such cases.

bad.name: Co-pay (Mandatory)
bad.quote: (21) Mandatory Co-payment: A mandatory Co-payment as specified in the Policy Schedule shall apply to all payable claims amount in respect of an Insured Person. Conditions i. For persons who have opted for a ‘Waiver of Mandatory Co-payment’ this Co-payment will not apply.
bad.reference: Section C.I.(21) Mandatory Co-payment + Section V (38) Waiver of Mandatory Co-payment
bad.explanation: A mandatory co-payment applies to all payable claims as per the Policy Schedule, unless a waiver is opted. This reduces every claim payout by the co-pay percentage and increases your out-of-pocket cost.

bad.name: Co-pay (PPN)
bad.quote: (37) Preferred Provider Network (PPN) Discount: ... discount of 10% on the premium payable... If ... treatment ... in a Hospital other than those listed as “Preferred Provider Network”, then ... shall bear a Co-Payment of 10% on each and every claim
bad.reference: Section V Optional Covers, (37) PPN Discount
bad.explanation: If the optional PPN discount is chosen, a 10% co-pay applies on each and every claim when treated outside the PPN hospital list. This can make claims meaningfully costlier despite the 10% premium discount.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: For Platinum - Essential Plan, treatment-wise sub-limits will apply as below... Cataract... Angioplasty... Knee replacement... Hip replacement... Cholecystectomy... hysterectomy...
bad.reference: Section C.I.(1) In-patient Hospitalization — Sub-limits table
bad.explanation: Treatment-wise sub-limits apply for procedures like cataract, angioplasty, knee/hip replacement, cholecystectomy and hysterectomy. Even with a high Sum Insured, payouts can be capped for these treatments, increasing your out-of-pocket spend.

unclear.name: PED Waiting Period
unclear.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of the number of months of continuous coverage ... as specified in the Policy Schedule / Certificate of Insurance / Product Benefit Table
unclear.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered only after a waiting period stated in the Policy Schedule/Certificate/Product Benefit Table, but the wording does not specify the months. Your PED coverage could start after 24/36/48 months depending on the variant you bought.

unclear.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
unclear.quote: (2) Pre – hospitalization Medical Expenses: ... for the number of days in accordance with the limits specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy
unclear.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for a number of days as per the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table, but the exact duration is not stated here. The number of covered days directly affects how much of your pre-admission tests and consultations get reimbursed.

unclear.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
unclear.quote: (3) Post – hospitalisation Medical Expenses: ... for the number of days in accordance with the limits specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy
unclear.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for a number of days as per the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table, but the exact duration is not stated here. A longer window is important for follow-up medicines, diagnostics and consultations after discharge.

unclear.name: Consumables
unclear.quote: Medicines, drugs and other allowable consumables prescribed by the treating Medical Practitioner; ... Annexure I – Non Medical Expenses
unclear.reference: Section C.I.(1)(vi) + Annexure I (Non-Medical Expenses list)
unclear.explanation: Allows medicines, drugs and other allowable consumables, while Annexure I lists non-medical items that are not payable. Your out-of-pocket cost will depend on which consumables the insurer treats as “allowable” versus excluded non-medical items.

unclear.name: No Claim Bonus
unclear.quote: We shall apply a Cumulative Bonus in the form of No Claim Bonus at such rates as specified in the Policy Schedule... In the event of a claim impacting the eligibility of a Cumulative Bonus, the accumulated Cumulative Bonus shall be reduced by the percentage of Sum Insured as accumulated in the previous Policy Year and as mentioned in Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table
unclear.explanation: No Claim Bonus applies at rates shown in the Policy Schedule, and on a claim the accumulated bonus is reduced as per the schedule rather than clearly stated here. The actual bonus growth and how much it drops after a claim will materially affect your effective Sum Insured over time.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
